title: Granular Response Profiles PRD — progressive rollout & acceptance checklist
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: PRD to define Granular Response Profiles (GRP): a first-class hosted-API feature that lets product teams declare deterministic, cost- and latency-aware response contracts per endpoint lane (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). Includes behavioral acceptance tests, telemetry gates, and a prescriptive progressive rollout checklist to minimize customer impact while shipping fine-grained lane semantics.
background: Customers want predictable output characteristics (verbosity, determinism, rerank stability) per use-case and the ability to ship progressive changes without causing regressions for high-value tenants. Current hosted endpoints surface global knobs (model, temperature) but lack an operable contract and rollout playbook for gradual behavior changes or for offering per-customer profiles with clear acceptance gates.
goals: Define canonical GRP schema: lane properties (intent profile, max tokens, deterministic_seed, cost_ceiling, fallback_model) for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank
Provide a behavioral test harness and eval prompts to catch regressions prior to rollout
Publish an operational rollout checklist with telemetry gating (error rate, latency P95, quality regressions) and per-slice rollback triggers
Ship UI controls in Console to create/assign GRPs to endpoints and customers (scope: control surface design, not final visual polish)
non_goals: Designing or training new models — GRPs will reference existing model variants
Full multi-tenant billing changes — only exposure of cost ceilings and telemetry; billing is separate work
Complete Console redesign — deliver functional controls, not final UX polish
in_scope: Schema for GRP (JSON contract) and server-side validation
Server-side enforcement of cost_ceiling and deterministic_seed behavior
Behavioral acceptance harness that runs generation + rerank checks against canonical prompt sets
Progressive rollout playbook (canary slices, metric gates, automatic fallback) and checklist
Console: minimal create/edit UI for GRPs and assignment to hosted endpoints/tenants
out_of_scope: Billing integrations to enforce cost_ceiling charging or alerts
Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) console UX changes — compatibility notes only
Model training or model-rewriting to satisfy GRP goals
requirements: REQ-1: GRP schema supports fields: name, lane (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank), model_preference (ordered list), deterministic_seed (optional int), temperature_range, max_output_tokens, cost_ceiling_usd_per_1k_tokens, fallback_policy (immediate/gradual/none), telemetry_tags
REQ-2: API accepts GRP references at endpoint creation time and resolves effective runtime profile (merge order: endpoint override > tenant profile > default profile)
REQ-3: Server must enforce cost_ceiling by triggering fallback_policy when projected cost estimate for a request exceeds the ceiling
REQ-4: Behavioral harness must include at least 30 canonical prompts per lane, with automated checks for: semantic similarity, hallucination rate heuristics, and rerank stability metrics
REQ-5: Console shows effective profile, last evaluation result, and ability to promote a GRP from staging to production
REQ-6: Telemetry: emit events for GRP_evaluation_result, GRP_rollout_step, GRP_fallback_triggered, and per-request profile_id; ensure these are queryable in Console and via API
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: GRP JSON schema documented and validated by server-side schema validator; sample GRP files included in PRD artifacts
AC-2: Unit & integration tests cover merge precedence logic (endpoint > tenant > default) with 95% branch coverage for resolution paths
AC-3: Behavioral harness run on staging passes with no more than +2% degradation in semantic-similarity metric vs baseline for 90% of prompts; any prompt with >5% drop must be triaged before rollout
AC-4: Runtime enforcement: simulated load tests show fallback_policy triggers correctly under cost-ceiling conditions for 100% of test requests designed to exceed ceiling
AC-5: Console MVP allows creating/editing/assigning GRPs; a staged GRP can be promoted and the promotion generates rollout events visible in telemetry within 30s

AC-6: Rollout gating: deploy to 5% canary slice; telemetry gates defined (error_rate <= 0.5%, latency_P95 <= baseline+50ms, quality_delta <= +2% semantic-similarity). If any gate fails, automatic pause and alert to SRE/PM occurs
AC-7: Release notes and runbook exist; on-call has a rollback playbook with specific commands and expected RTO (30 minutes)
launch_checklist: LC-1: PR with server/schema changes merged and deployed to staging
LC-2: Behavioral harness results attached to ticket and linked from Console evaluation tab
LC-3: Console MVP merged with feature-flag gating off by default
LC-4: Telemetry dashboards created: GRP adoption, fallback triggers, per-lane semantic similarity, P95 latency by profile
LC-5: SRE run chaos test for fallback paths and verify safe degradation behavior
LC-6: Documentation published (Confluence) with GRP contract examples and migration guide
LC-7: Support & Solutions teams briefed; canned responses and escalation flow prepared
LC-8: Final stakeholder sign-off (PM, Eng, SRE, Design) recorded in ticket
rollout_plan: Phase 0 — Internal validation: run behavioral harness against baseline models and log results; scope any prompt regressions
Phase 1 — Staging GRP smoke: assign staging endpoints and run canary harness (internal only)
Phase 2 — 5% external canary: picker based on stable low-risk customers; enable feature-flag for selector and monitor telemetry gates for 48 hours
Phase 3 — 25% ramp: if gates are green, ramp to 25% and run full eval sets including rerank stability and embeddings similarity
Phase 4 — Global: roll to 100% with automated monitoring, extended baseline comparisons and weekly quality regression checks
Rollback: immediate pause of rollout and revert to previous default profile if any telemetry gate breach persists for >15 minutes after mitigation steps
risks_mitigation: Risk: Quality regression for specific intents. Mitigation: Per-intent probe sets and conservative canary selection; block promotion if any probe falls beyond threshold
Risk: Increased latency due to enforcement logic. Mitigation: Benchmark enforcement in staging; add path to skip enforcement under overload and rely on fallback model
Risk: Customers confused by profile semantics. Mitigation: Clear Console copy, migration guides, and a pre-launch webinar for Solutions
Risk: Cost ceiling false positives causing excessive fallbacks. Mitigation: Use projected cost estimator with 95th percentile calibration; add conservative margin
open_questions: Q1: What is the canonical set of semantic-similarity metrics (embedding cosine vs ROUGE vs BERTScore) for each lane? (product + research decision)
Q2: Should deterministic_seed be enforced across batched requests that share KV cache? (eng feasibility)
Q3: How do we represent hybrid fallback policy (gradual throttling vs immediate swap) in the GRP schema? (policy design)
Q4: Do we expose per-tenant default GRPs in the public API or keep tenant assignment Console-only initially?
